\section[duḥkham]{\sk{दुःखम्} (duḥkham) — sorrow, pain}

\label{lesson:SA-C68-sorrow}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for rest, then the Sanskrit for ease.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{दुःखम्}}
\textbf{\sk{दुःखम्}} (\emph{duḥkham}) — \textquotedblleft{}sorrow\textquotedblright{}, the opposite of \textbf{\sk{सुखम्}}. The two words share their ending.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The other side of ease.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{duḥkham}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{duḥkham}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{duḥkham}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for rest, then the Sanskrit for ease, then say \emph{duḥkham} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{दुःखम्} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sorrow, pain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bhayam]{\sk{भयम्} (bhayam) — fear}

\label{lesson:SA-C68-fear}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for ease, then the Sanskrit for sorrow.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{भयम्}}
\textbf{\sk{भयम्}} (\emph{bhayam}) — \textquotedblleft{}fear\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{मम} \sk{भयम्} \sk{अस्ति}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am afraid\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What the dark brings.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for ease, then the Sanskrit for sorrow, then say \emph{bhayam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
